title: Night — Cannery Row Again
summary: The last beat of the session, delivered on the way to somewhere else. Forty feet of ordinary pavement between a chandler's and a shuttered bakery, and a dog that will not walk on it.

brief.wants: To get his spaniel to walk down the road, and to tell somebody about it because it has been happening every night.
brief.opensWith: Exasperation. He has already tried everything and he has an audience for the first time.

willDiscuss.note: It goes the long way round, up Fisher and back down, and it is a lazy animal, so that is saying something.
He has stood in it. There is nothing there.

voice.register: Ordinary, mildly aggrieved, entirely uninterested in anything larger than his own evening.
tics: Repeats 'every night' as though the repetition is the outrage
samples: "Every night. Every single night, this bit of pavement."
"He'll go round — he'll go the long way round, up Fisher and back down, and he's a lazy animal, so that's saying something."
"There's nothing there. I've looked. I've stood in it. There's nothing there."

beats.text: A man on Cannery Row having an argument with a spaniel that has stopped dead about forty feet up from the corner.
beats.readAloud:
There's a man on Cannery Row having an argument with a spaniel.

The dog has stopped dead about forty feet up from the corner and is doing the thing dogs do when they have made a decision — front legs braced, whole body committed to not being anywhere else.

when.condition: if a PC asks what the dog is doing

beats.text: If anyone uses the lens on this stretch of pavement, let them roll.

when.condition: if anyone thinks to use the lens here

beats.note: This is the highest reading they will get in Chapter One outside Founding Day, and it is on forty feet of nothing between a chandler's and a bakery.

beats.text: End the session on a man complaining about his dog, and roll credits.
beats.direction: Do not add a sting. Do not cut to anything. The last thing they hear is somebody's ordinary evening.

gmModifiers.label: The lens — local density
gmModifiers.note: Deliberately duplicated from the evening brief, same id and same table. A modifier that spans scenes has no campaign-level home yet — one brief per file means each scene that can roll it has to carry it. Worth fixing if a third scene needs the same table.

carryForward: Whether anyone used the lens on Cannery Row, and what they got.
notes: Nothing in this session resolves. That is correct. The party should end it with a map, a document that contradicts itself, a lead they didn't have time for, and one person at the table who saw something the others didn't.
